text:
Hi everyone 👋 
My partner Julia Gomes and I are a bit stuck and would love advice from anyone who's been through this. The situation:

I'm in Israel, and my partner Julia (Brazilian, non-married) is in Brazil. We submitted the online application in February at Misrad Hapnim Kfar Saba and completed documents in March.

On 20.05, our clerk at Misrad Hapnim sent an entry clearance ("הברקה") to the Israeli embassy in Brasília - but not as a "direct entry clearance," rather as an invitation to an embassy interview for a B/2 visa.

Julia contacted the embassy right away, sent everything the consular advisor asked for, and they've been "reviewing" for two weeks. Last Tuesday, he replied in writing:
"We can't estimate a timeline because we are **waiting for a response from Misrad Hapnim in Israel **regarding approval of the procedures."

I went back to our clerk at Misrad Hapnim. Her reply:
"What they needed to receive from us was the הברקה. Everything else is their internal matter. Everything that was up to me has been done."

So each side is now pointing at the other... I've got 2 questions:

1. Brazil is a visa-exempt country. According to AIC's guide, Julia should have received a direct entry clearance and been able to fly with her ETA-IL (which she already has), without the whole B/2 + embassy interview route (the guide states that route is for citizens of countries that DO require a tourist visa). Has this happened to anyone - that Kfar Saba routed you through the embassy even though your citizenship is visa-exempt? Is there a way to switch the route retroactively?
2. When Misrad Hapnim and the embassy are pointing at each other - what kind of follow-up actually works?

Any advice really appreciated 🙏
